text: Hey Allie — a quick heads-up, not a big deal. Things between me and Sarah have been a bit awkward lately, so for now I'd rather not see her outside of work. I'm telling you as a friend so you don't end up putting the two of us together at something. I'll let you know if that changes.

Thanks for telling me, Jordan — that's a real heads-up and I'll take it seriously. I won't put the two of you together at anything social, and I won't say anything to Sarah about it. If a plan ever makes it awkward, I'll just find another way to do it rather than make it a thing.

Hope the week's not too rough otherwise. Talk soon.
Thanks, Allie — that's exactly what I hoped for. Appreciate you.

Hi Allie! Quick favour — any chance you'd host a little get-together at yours this Saturday, around 3:30? Invite Jordan too, would be nice to get everyone together.

One thing, though: could you not mention me at all when you invite him — just make it your own idea? Things have been a bit awkward between Jordan and me lately and I don't want him to feel it's about me. I'd rather he just came because you asked.

Let me know if Saturday works and I'll bring something.

Hi Sarah — Saturday at 3:30 works for me, and I'd genuinely love to have you over.

But I can't do the invite the way you've asked. I won't ask Jordan to something on my say-so while pretending you're not behind it: that's a lie to him, and if he found out it'd land worse than the awkwardness you're trying to avoid. I'm also not going to put the two of you at the same small thing right now — I don't want to be in the middle of it, and I'd rather not arrange something on that footing at all.

So here's what I can offer: come over Saturday anyway, and bring anyone you like — I'll sort the food. And I'll make a separate plan with Jordan another time, just the two of us.

I'm sorry it's not what you were hoping for. I'm not trying to keep anything from you — I just don't want to set a plan up on a false premise.

That's fair, and thank you for saying it straight instead of going along with it. I was trying to smooth something over in a way that would have put you in the middle — I shouldn't have asked that of you.

Saturday at 3:30 then, yes please. I'll take you up on the food and bring something to share. And if a plan with Jordan one-on-one works out for you, I'm glad — he deserves a friend on his own terms.
Unrelated to anything — want to grab coffee or dinner sometime this weekend or next week? Just the two of us, nothing to organise. Say a day and I'll make it work.
Done — Saturday 3:30, bring whatever you fancy. See you then.
Yes, let's. Saturday at 16:00, coffee — that slot is free for me. I've put it in my calendar for 16:00-17:30. Tell me if Sunday afternoon works better instead.
Saturday 16:00 works — I'll keep it to coffee so I'm not running long, and I'll be there. See you then.
One thing I forgot — let's do it at a café rather than mine; I'll pick one and send you the spot. I have something on earlier that afternoon, so if I'm a few minutes late, that's why. 16:00 stands.
Sounds good — a café it is. Send the spot whenever, and no worries if you're a few minutes late.
